title: Standardize client retry signalling, hedged execution, and idempotency contracts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Different services and SDKs implement retries, timeouts, backoff, and hedged requests inconsistently. This leads to surprising duplicate side effects, variable latency under multi-region failover, and difficulty meeting token-level and per-route SLOs. Goal: Define and implement a single, minimal client-side contract for retry/timeout/backoff signaling and hedged execution semantics across Redwood services and official SDKs, plus a backwards-compatible migration strategy.
acceptance_criteria: A concise spec exists that defines: retryable vs non-retryable errors, idempotency key semantics for single-request and multipart flows, hedged request timing defaults, and agreement between SDKs and server-side routers.
All official SDKs (JS/Python/Go) expose the same configuration surface for retries, hedging, and idempotency keys and default to safe values that preserve SLOs.
Server-side router and runtime honor idempotency keys and hedging metadata; duplicate side-effects are prevented for documented idempotent endpoints.
Canary rollout shows no regression in P50/P95 latency and no increase in customer-visible duplicate side-effects in 2-week observation window.
Dashboards and alerts added: retry rate by route, hedged-request rate, idempotency-key conflicts, and client-side timeout overrides.
A migration runbook and SDK deprecation schedule published for customers who relied on previous default backoffs.
implementation_plan: Draft language for the client-server contract (JSON headers/metadata): 'Idempotency-Key', 'Retry-After-Policy', 'Hedged-Window-ms', and 'Client-Timeout-ms'. Keep headers minimal and human-readable.
Define error taxonomy for retry decisions: transient-network, server-overloaded, rate-limited (retryable with jitter), validation/auth errors (non-retryable). Publish mapping table.
Add server-side enforcement: when Idempotency-Key present for registered endpoints, persist request signature and reject or dedupe duplicates within configured TTL.
Implement hedged request support in runtime: accept 'Hedged-Window-ms' and schedule second replica after N ms; ensure KV-cache and token accounting correctly attribute cost to customer.
Add SDK primitives: Request.wrapWithIdempotency(key), Client.retryPolicy(config), Client.hedging(windowMs).
Implement telemetry hooks in SDKs to emit retry attempts, hedged attempts, and idempotency TTL violations to our telemetry endpoint.
Server and SDK integration tests: deterministic flaky network simulator, multi-region leader failover tests that exercise hedging and idempotency behavior.
Incremental rollout: default to conservative values (no hedging by default, safe retry limits) behind feature flags for 10% of traffic and expand after checks.
Create migration guide and compatibility shims for older SDKs that do not set idempotency keys.
Coordinate with Console to expose per-route controls and allow admins to opt endpoints into stronger idempotency enforcement.
Publish conformance test suite for partner/self-hosted deployments.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Spec & tests (Week 1-2): finalize contract doc, unit tests in SDKs, runtime feature flagged implementation.
Phase 1 - Internal canary (Week 3): enable on 5% internal traffic, e2e multi-region failover injection, observe metrics for 72h.
Phase 2 - Customer beta (Week 4-5): opt-in by project in Console, maintain detailed duplicates and cost dashboards, gather feedback.
Phase 3 - Gradual default switch (Week 6-8): increase to 50% then 100% traffic, enable hedging only where latency SLOs benefit and idempotency enabled server-side.
Phase 4 - Hardening & docs (Week 9-10): promote SDK docs, migration runbook, add automated checks to CI for new endpoints.
Rollback plan: immediate feature-flag disable; automatic kill switch if duplicate side-effects metric exceeds threshold or customer complaints spike.
decisions: Hedging will be opt-in per-route by default; default hedged-window is 0ms for safety. We will allow customers to opt-in via Console to enable hedging with server-side idempotency enforcement.
Idempotency is a first-class signal: server persists a request fingerprint for a configurable TTL (default 24 hours) for endpoints registered as 'idempotent'.
SDKs will not retry non-idempotent write endpoints by default; SDKs will expose an explicit 'allowUnsafeRetries' flag for advanced use-cases with documented risk.
Client-side timeouts are advisory: server may apply its own deadline and return explicit error codes to guide retries rather than silently allowing long client timeouts.
Use consistent exponential backoff with capped jitter across SDKs; defaults tuned to preserve latency SLOs under overload rather than maximizing success rate.
Telemetry will attribute hedged-request cost to the originating customer and report per-token accounting for billing transparency.
risks: If idempotency TTL is too short, legitimate retries across region failover may be treated as duplicates; if too long, storage overhead increases.
Hedging increases overall token cost; we must avoid default hedging that surprises customers and increases bills.
Backward compatibility: older SDKs that always retried aggressively may cause duplicate side-effects until migrated.
Edge cases around multipart or streaming endpoints where idempotency semantics are harder to define and enforce.
Operational complexity: additional state for persisted idempotency records and new telemetry dimensions could increase SRE burden.
qa_tests: Unit tests for SDK retry policy normalization and header propagation across JS/Python/Go.
Integration test: multi-region request routing with simulated region failure and hedged replica arriving after configured window; verify single side-effect when idempotency-key present.
Chaos test: increase server overload and verify backpressure causes clients to adapt rather than saturate (load-shedding + client abort paths).
Performance test: measure P50/P95/P99 latency and tail behavior with and without hedging on representative workloads.
Cost analysis: run billing-sim to estimate token cost delta for hedging enabled at 10/50/100 percent traffic.
Security test: ensure idempotency keys cannot be abused for replay attacks; rotate any signing keys used for request fingerprinting.
